messages.author: f28bbf1544c274f8
messages.subject: inbreed or outbreed
parts:
Hi, 
I have a data of 283 F2 fish. These were obtained from a single pair of F1 parent and F0 grand parent. The F0 was obtained from natural population (mother from marine and father from pond) and the genotypes are not  homogeneous and some are unknown (e.g., A- and BC; "-"= unknown). Alleles are differing with the loci (e.g., allele of the some of the locus is A and B, for some is A, B and C and some contains A, B, C and D. 
What should I call for analyzing my data in R/qtl? inbreed or out breed? The R/qtl is recognizing my data set as "four way cross" and I am able to do the most of the analysis in it. But, I am in a bit of hesitation, if I am heading in the right direction?  Please help me in defining my data set. 
Best regards, 
Mehedi

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] inbreed or outbreed
parts:
This should be treated as a phase-known 4-way cross. You need to use the genotypes in the F0 grandparents to infer phase in the F1 parents, and then read it into R/qtl using the genotype encodings described in the help file for the read.cross function. But if R/qtl has recognized it as a 4-way cross, it seems that you have already figured that part out.

We call it a 4-way cross, thinking of the four grandparents of the two outbred parents, even though in your case the 4 grandparents are really just two individuals repeated twice. There are potentially four alleles at any one locus: the four haplotypes in the two F1 parents.

karl
